BURHAN:v1p305/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p305/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p305/r5.claim: He rejects strained parsing that makes للفقراء a substitute for ولذي القربى, driven by the Hanafi rule that kinship alone gives no entitlement, or makes الذين ظلموا a substitute for للناس.
BURHAN:v1p305/r5.anchor: الرابع تجنب الأعاريب التى هى خلاف الظاهر والمنافية لنظم الكلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r1.claim: Surat al-Anbiyāʾ argues that the Hour is real and near, even through death, and that judgment will encompass both the great and the insignificant.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r1.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على تحقق الساعة وقربها ولو بالموت ، ووقوع الحساب فيها على الجليل والحقير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r2.claim: The Creator has no partner able to impede the Hour and never breaks his word; the prophets' stories collectively establish this, though no single story plainly proves every point by itself.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63/r2.anchor: والدال على ذلك أوضح دلالة مجموع قصص جماعة ممن ذكر فيها من الأنبياء

JISHUMI:v7p4801/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r4.claim: The question that God is not questioned about His acts connects to the approaching reckoning: people will be asked whether they thanked or rejected His blessings.
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r4.anchor: إنه يتصل بقوله: (اقترب للناس حسابهم) والحساب هو السؤال عما أنعم عليهم

ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r1.claim: According to the Itqan, this Meccan surah belongs to the final group of Meccan revelations; its title reflects its repeated references to earlier prophets.
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r1.anchor: which according to the 'Itqan belongs to the last group of the Meccan revelations

ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r2.claim: The surah’s main theme is God’s oneness, uniqueness, and transcendence as the core of prophetic revelation, a truth people often forget or ignore.
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r2.anchor: the core of all prophetic revelation

ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r3.claim: The prophets’ stories show the continuity and unity of revelation and religious experience; belief in one God entails one community and brotherhood among true believers across outward labels.
ASAD-NOTES:21:intro/r3.anchor: this community of yours is one single community, since I am the Sustainer of you all

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r1.claim: The revelation brought by this prophet matches earlier revelation; rejecting it repeats the fate of nations that mocked and rejected their messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r1.anchor: The reminder they needed for the conclusive communication of the truth has

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r1.claim: The sūrah opens without introduction because it completes the previous sūrah's warning; their opening and closing verses dovetail, a proximity discussed in the explanation of al-Tawbah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r1.anchor: it actually is a completion of the subject of warning on which the previous sūrah ended

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r2.speaker: Ibn ‘Abbās
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r2.claim: “People” refers to the idolaters of Makkah; using a general term while they evade God's reminder conveys aversion and regret.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r2.anchor: the Idolaters of Makkah, as is the opinion of Ibn ‘Abbās (rta)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r3.claim: The near accountability is factual: after a messenger conclusively communicates truth, a nation has one option, faith; refusal brings destruction, and heedlessness with evasion compounds guilt.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p94/r3.anchor: after conclusive communication of the truth, it is necessarily wiped out

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r4.claim: Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ is Meccan without disagreement.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r5.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh counts al-Kahf, Maryam, Ṭā Hā, and al-Anbiyāʾ among the earliest suras he learned, an old, accumulated portion of the Qur’an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r5.anchor: وعن عبد الله: الكهف، ومريم، وطه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r6.claim: The sura answers Quraysh’s reaction to the preceding warning of reckoning: they said Muhammad’s promised resurrection and judgment were false or far off, so God revealed that their reckoning had drawn near.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r6.anchor: ومناسبة هذه السورة لما قبلها أنه لما ذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r7.claim: اقترب has the basic sense of قرب, though some consider it more emphatic because of its augmented form; الناس may mean Meccan polytheists or all deniers of resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r7.anchor: واقترب افتعل بمعنى الفعل المجرد وهو قرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r8.claim: The approaching reckoning means the Hour’s time; حساب can mean measuring an amount or the amount counted. What is coming is near despite a long wait, near to God, or near relative to the shorter future than past.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p405/r8.anchor: واقتراب الحساب اقتراب وقته والحساب في اللغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r1.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r1.claim: The Prophet says he and the Hour were sent like these two fingers, indicating nearness; a poet similarly says the hoped-for one is nearer than tomorrow and the feared one farther than yesterday.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says للناس either attaches directly to اقترب or emphasizes that the reckoning belongs to them; the author rejects the second as unattested and syntactically problematic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هذه اللام لا تخلو من أن تكون صلة لاقترب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r3.claim: He objects that the possession-emphasis analysis has no recognized parallel here, lacks a governor if attached to the genitive source, and should follow the emphasized phrase; لَأبا لك is exceptional and not a model.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p406/r4.claim: The wāw in وهم is circumstantial. Their heedlessness and turning away are compatible: they fail to consider consequences, then ignore reminders when awakened from inattention.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r1.claim: The surah's purpose is to prove the Hour's certainty and nearness, even through death, and the judgment of both eminent and lowly; the unique Creator cannot be prevented and does not alter his promise.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r1.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على تحقق الساعة وقربها ولو بالموت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r2.claim: The combined prophetic stories provide the proof: no single story independently establishes every aspect, but each points to part of it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r2.anchor: ولا يستقل قصة منها استقلالا ظاهرا بجميع ذلك كما سنبين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r5.claim: Taha expands Moses' story, only briefly treated in Maryam; al-Anbiya then details prophets not narrated in Maryam and briefly recalls several already mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r5.anchor: أنه سبحانه لما ذكر في سورة مريم قصص عدة من الأنبياء عليهم السلام وبعضها مبسوط

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r1.claim: Since spatial nearness is impossible here, the nearness is temporal: the time of people’s reckoning has approached.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r1.anchor: القرب لا يعقل إلا في المكان والزمان

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r2.claim: One answer to the apparent delay is that the reckoning is near in God’s measure, as 22:47 says a day with God is like a thousand years.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r2.anchor: أنه مقترب عند الله تعالى والدليل عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r3.claim: Another answer is that every event still to come is near however long its wait; only what has passed is distant, as the cited verse says.

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r4.claim: A deadline is called near once more time has elapsed than remains; by that measure the Hour is near because less of the period of obligation remains than has passed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r4.anchor: إذا كان الماضي أكثر من الباقي

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r5.claim: The Prophet compared his mission and the Hour to two fingers as evidence of their closeness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r5.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( بعثت أنا والساعة كهاتين )

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r6.claim: The text reports the claim that the Prophet sealed prophethood because less of the period of religious obligation remained than had elapsed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r6.anchor: وهذا الوجه قيل إنه عليه السلام ختم به النبوة

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r7.claim: Mentioning the Hour’s nearness benefits those bound by the law by moving them to repent and free themselves from sins.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r7.anchor: إنما ذكر تعالى هذا الاقتراب لما فيه من المصلحة للمكلفين فيكون أقرب إلى تلافي الذنوب والتحرر عنها

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r8.claim: The time is left unspecified because concealment is more beneficial, just as concealing the time of death is.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r8.anchor: إنما لم يعين الوقت لأجل أن كتمانه أصلح

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r9.claim: Calling the Resurrection the Day of Reckoning emphasizes that accounting exposes a person’s state and makes the warning more frightening.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r9.anchor: الفائدة في تسمية يوم القيامة بيوم الحساب أن الحساب هو الكاشف عن حال المرء فالخوف من ذكره أعظم

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r10.claim: People here means those who are subject to reckoning, the morally responsible, rather than those with no part in it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r10.anchor: يجب أن يكون المراد بالناس من له مدخل في الحساب وهم المكلفون دون من لا مدخل له

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the people as the polytheists; the generic term denotes only part of its class because the following description concerns polytheists.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المراد بالناس المشركون

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r12.claim: Their heedlessness is failure to remember or consider the reckoning and their fate, despite reason requiring recompense for good and evil.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r12.anchor: غافلون عن حسابهم ساهون لا يتفكرون في عاقبتهم مع اقتضاء عقولهم أنه لا بد من جزاء المحسن والمسيء

RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r13.claim: When signs and warnings awaken them from heedlessness, they turn away and block their ears.
RAZI-FULL:v22p120/r13.anchor: إذا انتبهوا من سنة الغفلة ورقدة الجهالة مما يتلى عليهم من الآيات والنذر أعرضوا وسدوا أسماعهم

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r1.claim: The opening verse of al-Anbiyāʾ announces that the time of reckoning is approaching.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r1.anchor: The first verse of al-Anbiyāʾ announces that the time of the reckoning approaches (R)

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r2.claim: Ḥisāb denotes the accounting of the Day of Judgment, also called the Day of Reckoning.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r2.anchor: is a word used to signify the accounting of the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r3.speaker: some theologians (Q, Z)
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r3.claim: Some theologians say more time has passed since creation than remains until the world’s end.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r3.anchor: Some theologians have said that the time that has passed since God created the world is greater

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r4.claim: The chronological argument rests on iqtaraba ordinarily indicating that one is closer to one’s destination than one’s origin.

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r5.speaker: M
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r5.claim: From God’s perspective reckoning is near in relation to His knowledge, not temporally, since He knows all moments simultaneously; humans think it distant.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r5.anchor: from God’s point of view the reckoning is close—not in a temporal sense, because God knows all moments simultaneously—but rather is close with regard to His Knowledge

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r6.claim: Commentators say each person’s certain death is reason enough to regard reckoning as near, regardless of when the world ends.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r6.anchor: part of what is signified by their reckoning draws nigh (Q)

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r7.speaker: Ṭ, Q
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r7.claim: Being heedless means caring only for this world and paying no attention to the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r7.anchor: To be heedless means that people only care about this world (Ṭ) and pay no attention to the matters of the Hereafter (Q)

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r8.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r8.claim: Sufis distinguish those heedless through worldly engrossment from righteous believers mindful of the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r8.anchor: there are those who are heedless of the Hereafter because they are engrossed in worldly affairs, and there are the righteous believers who are mindful

STUDYQURAN:21:1/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r9.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r9.claim: Another kind of heedlessness arises from being so absorbed in remembrance of God that one gives no thought to the Garden or Fire.
STUDYQURAN:21:1/r9.anchor: there are also those who are heedless of the Hereafter because they are so engrossed in the remembrance of God that they give no thought to the Garden

TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r1.claim: People's reckoning draws near: they will be questioned about their deeds and blessings, and whether they obeyed or disobeyed God in them.
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r1.anchor: إياهم ماذا عملوا فيها، وهل أطاعوه فيها

TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r2.claim: In worldly life they disregard the approaching reckoning, failing to reflect, prepare, or make ready because they do not grasp its severe trials and terrors.
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r2.anchor: وقد أعرضوا عن ذلك، فتركوا الفكر فيه، والاستعداد له والتأهب، جهلا منهم بما هم لاقوه عند ذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet explained their heedlessness as being in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v16p221#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:21:1/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r1.claim: The sūra treats prophethood on the foundations of monotheism and resurrection: it opens with approaching judgment and heedlessness, then answers mockery through earlier prophets, their stories, judgment, and the victory of the pious.
TABATABAI:21:1/r1.anchor: الكلام حول النبوة بانيا ذلك على التوحيد والمعاد فتفتتح بذكر اقتراب الحساب وغفلة الناس عن ذلك

TABATABAI:21:1/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r2.claim: The sūra moves from accusations that the Prophet is a magician, dreamer, fabricator, or poet to the shared qualities and message of earlier prophets, then to judgment and the pious inheriting the earth.
TABATABAI:21:1/r2.anchor: واستهزاء الناس بنبوة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ورميهم إياه بأنه ساحر بل ما أتى به أضغاث أحلام

TABATABAI:21:1/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r3.claim: Its principal emphasis is warning and threat rather than promise and glad tidings; its Meccan origin is undisputed and confirmed by its flow.
TABATABAI:21:1/r3.anchor: والغلبة في السورة للوعيد على الوعد وللإنذار على التبشير.

TABATABAI:21:1/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r4.claim: Iqtaraba and qaruba both mean “draw near,” but the expanded form is stronger and conveys greater attention to the nearness.
TABATABAI:21:1/r4.anchor: الاقتراب افتعال من القرب واقترب وقرب بمعنى واحد غير أن اقترب أبلغ لزيادة بنائه

TABATABAI:21:1/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r5.claim: Qaruba and iqtaraba take min or ilā; min measures nearness from the object, while ilā measures it from the subject, as min marks origin and ilā endpoint.
TABATABAI:21:1/r5.anchor: ويتعدى القرب والإقتراب بمن وإلى يقال قرب أو اقترب زيد من عمرو أو إلى عمرو

TABATABAI:21:1/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r6.claim: The lām means “toward” (ilā), not “from” (min): the verse pictures the reckoning itself approaching people who are heedless.
TABATABAI:21:1/r6.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن اللام في { للناس } بمعنى إلى لا بمعنى من

TABATABAI:21:1/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r7.claim: The reckoning is God's actual accounting of people's deeds on Judgment Day, not a metonym for its time or an omitted word meaning “time of reckoning.”
TABATABAI:21:1/r7.anchor: والمراد بالحساب - وهو محاسبة الله سبحانه أعمالهم يوم القيامة - نفس الحساب لا زمانه

TABATABAI:21:1/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:21:1/r8.claim: Some insist that the verse means the time of reckoning; another explanation says nearness properly belongs to time and only indirectly to events occurring in it, which the author rejects here.
TABATABAI:21:1/r8.anchor: وإن أصر بعضهم عليه ووجهه بعض آخر بأن الزمان هو الأصل في القرب والبعد

TABATABAI:21:1/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r9.claim: The warning recalls accountability for deeds: wisdom requires a divine reminder, and people must heed it seriously rather than play or let their hearts be distracted.
TABATABAI:21:1/r9.anchor: لأن الغرض في المقام متعلق بتذكرة نفس الحساب لتعلقه بأعمال الناس إذ كانوا مسؤولين عن أعمالهم

TABATABAI:21:1/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1/r10.claim: If the passage aimed to describe the Hour's terrors and punishment, it would more fittingly say “Day of Reckoning” or explicitly refer to its time.
TABATABAI:21:1/r10.anchor: نعم لو كان الكلام مسوقا لبيان أهوال الساعة وما أعد من العذاب للمجرمين كان الأنسب التعبير بيوم الحساب

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r1.claim: Successive reciters produce distinct sound tokens resembling the original utterance; they are not numerically the same sounds except by convention and loose usage.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r1.anchor: ثم إن الذي تكلم به قائل القول الأول ثانيا والذي تكلم به الناقل الذي ينقله

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r2.claim: Sounds count as speech only when conventionally made signs for mental meanings; they count as one utterance only by treating their intended purpose as one.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r2.anchor: وليست هذه الأصوات كلاما إلا من حيث إنها علائم وأمارات بحسب الوضع والإعتبار تدل على معان ذهنية،

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r3.claim: Speech qua speech is a conventional construct without external existence; only the sounds exist, and calling the construct actual is metaphorical.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r3.anchor: ويتحصل بذلك أن الكلام بما أنه كلام أمر وضعي اعتباري لا تحقق له في الخارج من ظرف الدعوى والإعتبار،

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r4.claim: Because speech as a convention is not an external reality, it has neither temporal origination nor endurance nor eternity, which apply to externally existing things.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r4.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن الكلام لا يتصف بشيء من الحدوث والبقاء فإن الحدوث وهو مسبوقية الوجود بالعدم الزماني

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r5.claim: Eternal speech made of ordered letters is impossible: succession entails that a later letter follows and is preceded, contradicting eternity.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r5.anchor: وهو أن الكلام هو المؤلف من حروف مترتبة متدرجة بعضها قبل وبعضها بعد،

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r6.claim: Speech in its proper conventional sense is neither a real action nor an essential attribute of the speaker; only its external sounds are acts, and “speaking” is attributed by extension.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r6.anchor: لا ريب أن الكلام بحسب الحقيقة ليس فعلا ولا صفة للمتكلم لأنه أمر اعتباري لا تحقق له إلا في ظرف الدعوى والوضع

TABATABAI:21:1-15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r7.claim: The terms speaking and causing speech are extended from the speaker's production of sounds, as with conventional relations such as reverence, insult, buying, and selling.
TABATABAI:21:1-15/r7.anchor: ثم يؤخذ عن نسبته إلى الفاعل وصف له وهو التكلم والتكليم كما في نظائره من الاعتباريات

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r1.claim: Analyzed by its purpose of revealing hidden mental meanings, speech can be treated as real; this approach also applies to conventional ideas such as prostration, obedience, sovereignty, and the Book.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r1.anchor: من الممكن أن يحلل الكلام من جهة غرضه وهو الكشف عن المعاني المكنونة في الضمير

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r2.claim: Speech is what reveals what is hidden in the mind; every effect reveals its cause's latent perfection, and essential attributes reveal an object's hidden essence.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r2.anchor: فحقيقة الكلام هو ما يكشف به عن مكنونات الضمير فكل معلول لعلته لكشفه بوجوده عن كمالها المكنون في ذاتها،

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r3.speaker: الفلاسفة
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r3.claim: Philosophers call God's essential attributes—knowledge, power, and life—His speech, and also call the world His speech because it reveals Him.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الذي يذكر الفلاسفة أن صفاته تعالى الذاتية

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r4.claim: Under this analysis, speech's temporal status follows its mode of being: divine knowledge is eternal, created Zayd is an originated sign, and revelation is originated as imparted but eternal as divine knowledge.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r4.anchor: فالعلم الإلهي كلام قديم بقدم الذات وزيد الحادث بما هو آية تكشف عن ربه كلام له حادث،

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r5.claim: The recited Qur'an as conventional, meaningful verses is neither eternal nor originated in itself, though its sounds originate; its true meanings as known by God are eternal with His knowledge.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r5.anchor: إن أريد به هذه الآيات التي نتلوها بما أنها كلام دال على معان ذهنية نظير سائر الكلام ليس بحسب الحقيقة لا حادثا ولا قديما

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r6.claim: The created-versus-eternal debate is unproductive: eternal recited sounds are impossible, while eternal divine knowledge needs no separate Qur'an attribute beyond knowledge.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r6.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن البحث عن قدم القرآن وحدوثه بما أنه كلام الله مما لا جدوى فيه

TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r7.claim: If every analysis that reduces to a divine attribute counted as a separate essential attribute, the list would be limitless; scripture's use of “speech” refers plainly to the first, recited sense.
TABATABAI:21:1-15#2/r7.anchor: على أنه لا موجب حينئذ لعد الكلام صفة ثبوتية ذاتية أخرى له تعالى وراء العلم لرجوعه إليه

THALABI:v6p268#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p268#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p268#3/r1.claim: The lām in the opening means min: God's reckoning of people for their deeds has drawn near.
THALABI:v6p268#3/r1.anchor: اقترب للناس قيل: اللام بمعنى من أي اقترب من الناس حسابهم محاسبة الله

THALABI:v6p268#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p268#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p268#3/r2.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they are heedless of the reckoning, turning away from thinking about it and preparing for it.
THALABI:v6p268#3/r2.anchor: وهم واو الحال في غفلة عنه معرضون عن التفكير فيه والتأهب له

THALABI:v6p268#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p268#3/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p268#3/r3.claim: The verse was revealed about those who deny the resurrection.
THALABI:v6p268#3/r3.anchor: عن التفكير فيه والتأهب له، نزلت في منكري البعث.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r1.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says qaruba and iqtaraba have the same basic sense, but the iftaʿala form is more emphatic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r1.anchor: قال المبرد: هما (¬2) واحد، إلا أن افتعل مؤكد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r2.claim: The reckoning is near in that little time remains before it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى الاقتراب هاهنا: قصر (¬4) المدة التي بينهم وبين الحساب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies “the people” as the people of Mecca.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {للناس} قال الكلبي: يعني أهل مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r4.claim: The exegetes take their reckoning as God’s accounting them for their deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r4.anchor: {حسابهم} قال المفسرون: محاسبة الله إياهم على أعمالهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, interprets the reckoning as punishment, since one whose account is examined is punished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء، عن ابن عباس (¬3): يريد عذابهم: لأن من نوقش الحساب عذب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the phrase means that the time of their reckoning has drawn near.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المعنى -والله أعلم-: اقترب للناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r7.claim: On this reading, the verse refers to the Resurrection, as in 54:1, “the Hour has drawn near.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r7.anchor: كما قال في سورة أخرى: {اقتربت الساعة} [القمر: 1]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r8.claim: The People of Meanings give two grounds for calling the reckoning near: everything coming is near, or it is near compared with the time already elapsed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p7#2/r8.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: واقتراب (¬2) حسابهم يحمل على أحد معنيين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {في غفلة} قال الكلبي: جهالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r2.claim: The exegetes say the people are heedless of what God will do to them on that Day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r2.anchor: وقال المفسرون: عما الله فاعل بهم ذلك اليوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r3.claim: They turn away from preparing for the reckoning.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, says they turn away from what Muhammad brought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p9/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: أعرضوا عما جاء به

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r1.claim: The reckoning is the Resurrection, when God will account people for their deeds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r1.anchor: وقت محاسبة الله إياهم على أعمالهم. يعني: القيامة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r2.claim: They are heedless of preparing for that Day and turn away from faith.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:1-3/r2.anchor: عن التأهب لذلك { معرضون } عن الإيمان

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r1.anchor: قوله: {اقترب للناس حسابهم} [الأنبياء: 1] أي: إن ذلك قريب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r2.claim: The Prophet compared his coming and the Hour to adjacent fingers, identified by the narrators as the middle and index fingers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r2.anchor: حدثني أبو الأشهب والمبارك عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إنما مثلي ومثل الساعة كهاتين فما فضل إحداهما على الأخرى» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r3.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī reports the Prophet warning that the angel of the Trumpet already holds it at his mouth, awaiting God's command to blow.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r3.anchor: عن أبي عمران الجوني قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «حين بعث إلي، بعث إلى صاحب الصور، فأهوى به إلى فيه وقدم رجلا، وأخر أخرى، متى يؤمر ينفخ، ألا فاتقوا النفخة» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r4.claim: The heedless, turning-away people are polytheists, heedless of the Hereafter and turned away from the Qur'an.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p297/r4.anchor: {وهم في غفلة معرضون} [الأنبياء: 1] يعني المشركين في غفلة من الآخرة معرضون عن القرآن.

QASHANI:21:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:1/r1.claim: The accounting draws near in the minor resurrection; if people understood resurrection, they would witness their accounting now.
QASHANI:21:1/r1.anchor: { اقترب للناس حسابهم } في القيامة الصغرى، بل لو عرفوا القيامة لعاينوا حسابهم الآن

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r1.claim: God created the world, life, and death as a test of who does the best deeds, gave people countless blessings, and asks them to thank Him, obey His commands, and avoid His prohibitions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r1.anchor: Yüce Allah dünyayı, hayatı ve ölümü imtihan için yani kimin daha güzel işler yapacağını ortaya çıkarmak için yaratmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r2.claim: The verse warns that people will soon be called to account for those blessings and urges them to prepare for that day.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r2.anchor: Âyet-i kerîmede, insanların bu nimetlerden bir gün hesaba çekileceği ve o günün yaklaştığı haber verilerek uyarılmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r3.claim: A believer is heedless when, despite believing in the afterlife, they fail to prepare, avoid sin, repent, fulfill worship carefully, or do good works.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r3.anchor: Müminin gaflette bulunması, âhiret gününe iman ettiği halde orası için gereken hazırlığı yapmadığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r4.claim: A disbeliever is heedless when they ignore their creator, purpose, and accountability for good and evil, and turn away from warnings by prophets and revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r4.anchor: İnkârcının gaflette bulunması ise kendini yaratan bir aşkın kudretin bulunduğunu, başı boş bir varlık olarak yaratılmış olmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r5.claim: The verse uses the past tense because the Day of Judgment is certain to come.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:1/r5.anchor: hesap günü kesinkes geleceği için âyette geçmiş zaman şekli kullanılmıştır

QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r1.claim: God's mighty name grants beautiful favor to obedience and respite to neglect; return and confession bring remembrance, sin is concealed, repentance is met with mercy, and arrogance is crushed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r1.anchor: إن أطاع فضله ، وإن أضاع أمهله

QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r2.claim: Outward illumination comes from God's enabling, while inner illumination comes from His realization; enabling gives worshippers spiritual striving, and realization gives knowers complete witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r2.anchor: ما استنارت الظواهر إلا بآثار توفيقه ، وما استضاءت السرائر إلا بأنوار تحقيقه

QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r3.claim: Complete spiritual striving earns future recompense, while abiding in witnessing wins immediate nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r3.anchor: وبتمام مجاهدتهم وجدوا آجل مثوبتهم ، وبدوام مشاهدتهم نالوا عاجل قربتهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r4.claim: Among people, the obedient merit a great reward from God, and the disobedient deserve His punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r4.anchor: فالمطيعون منهم عظم لدينا ثوابهم ، والعاصون منهم حق منا عقابهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r5.claim: One heedlessness is absorption in worldly life and desire, a mark of alienation whose sufferers awaken only at death.
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r5.anchor: غافل عن حسابه باستغراقه في دنياه وهواه

QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r6.claim: A second heedlessness is absorption in the Lord, a quality of union; these people never return from ecstatic absence because they are effaced in divine existence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p285/r6.anchor: غافل عن حسابه لاستهلاكه في مولاه

BURHAN:v1p179/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.claim: Zarkashi classifies declarative clauses as a type of sūra opening, listing al-Anbiya, al-Qamar and al-Rahman among twenty-three such sūras.
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.anchor: الرابع الجمل الخبرية نحو ﴿ يسألونك عن الأنفال ﴾ ﴿ براءة من الله ﴾

SULAMI:v2p3#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r1.claim: The time to awaken has drawn near, yet people remain heedless of repentance, vigilance, and awakening.
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : دنا أوان الانتباه ، وهم في غفلة معرضون عن طريق التوبة والتيقظ والانتباه .

SULAMI:v2p3#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r2.speaker: عبد العزيز المكي
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r2.claim: Most life has passed and the rest will soon pass in heedlessness; regret remains, but persistent sins have blinded hearts to warning and promised punishment.
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r2.anchor: قال عبد العزيز المكي : الاقتراب يدل على مضي الأكثر ، ومضي الأقل عن قريب كما مضى الأكثر ،

SULAMI:v2p3#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r3.claim: People should reckon and weigh themselves before judgment, since prophetic warnings leave no excuse; blessed is the one who wakes before being awakened.
SULAMI:v2p3#4/r3.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : جاز لك أن تحاسب نفسك وقد مضى أكثر عمرك ، وتنزجر عن الغفلة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p234#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p234#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p234#3/r1.claim: The approaching reckoning is the nearness of the Resurrection, while people remain heedless.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p234#3/r1.anchor: {اقترب للناس حسابهم} أي قربت القيامة {وهم في غفلة}

SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r1.claim: The lām in للناس is syntactically attached to اقترب.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r1.anchor: قوله: { اقترب للناس }: اللام متعلق ب " اقترب ".

SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers the lām either as a complement of اقترب or as emphasis of the حسابهم possessive relation, comparing أزف للحي رحيلهم and related constructions; he calls the latter more unusual.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هذه اللام لا تخلو: إما أن تكون صلة لاقترب، أو تأكيدا لإضافة الحساب إليهم

SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r3.claim: The Shaykh rejects the possessive-emphasis analysis: it lacks a known precedent, leaves the lām without a governor, conflicts with the order of an emphasized element, and differs from the cited examples; لا أبا لك is disputed and anomalous.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ:/ " يعني بقوله صلة لاقترب أي: متعلقة به. وأما جعله اللام

SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r4.claim: The author says al-Zamakhshari's account resembles لا أبا لك and preserves its correct meaning; its difficulty follows the majority's account of that construction, so its established analysis can support the analogy.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1/r4.anchor: قلت: مسألة الزمخشري أشبه شيء بمسألة " لا أبا لك " ، والمعنى الذي أورده صحيح.

SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase may depend on an omitted expression as a circumstantial phrase from the pronoun in معرضون.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { وهم في غفلة معرضون } يجوز أن يكون الجار متعلقا بمحذوف على أنه حال من الضمير

SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls في غفلة a second predicate, while the author explains that it is first in the actual order and only second by treating its meaning as a single word.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r2.anchor: وقول أبي البقاء في هذا الجار " إنه خبر ثان " يعني في العدد،

SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r3.claim: The whole clause وهم في غفلة معرضون is a circumstantial clause describing للناس.
SAMIN-DURR:21:1#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الجملة في محل نصب على الحال من " للناس ".

ZAJJAJ:v3p383/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p383/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p383/r1.claim: The reckoning has drawn near for people; more precisely, the time of their reckoning is near.

ASAD-NOTES:21:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:1#n1/r1.claim: Asad's literal rendering is “and yet in their heedlessness they are obstinate.”
ASAD-NOTES:21:1#n1/r1.anchor: Lit., "and yet in [their] heedlessness they are obstinate (mu'ridun)"

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Anbiyā’ pairs with Ṭāhā and opens where that sūrah ended: a warning that Quraysh’s demanded punishment sign is near.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r1.anchor: This sūrah forms a pair with Sūrah Ṭāhā, the previous sūrah. It begins on the same note on which the last sūrah ended.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r2.claim: At the end of Ṭāhā, Quraysh were told to wait if they insisted on seeing a punishment sign, since punishment was near.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r2.anchor: if they insist on seeing a sign of the punishment, then they should wait because the punishment is at hand.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r3.claim: After the Messenger’s advent, Quraysh’s accountability is imminent, yet they remain absorbed in frivolities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r3.anchor: the time of accountability of the Quraysh is now imminent but they are engrossed in frivolties.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r4.claim: They mock the Prophet and revelation, calling him sorcerer, magician, poet, or impostor, or dismissing revelation as wayward dreams.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r4.anchor: Some call him a sorcerer, some a magician, some a poet and an imposter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r5.claim: They demand miracles from the Prophet like those performed by earlier prophets.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r5.anchor: They demand from him similar miracles as the ones worked by previous prophets.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r6.claim: They regard the world as amusement created to entertain its Creator.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r6.anchor: They regard this world to be a place of amusement created to entertain the creator.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r7.claim: Their trust rests on self-created idols that are figments of their imagination.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r7.anchor: All their trust hinges on their self-created idols. The fact is that these are figments of their own imagination.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r8.claim: God’s prophets have no connection with these imagined idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r8.anchor: Prophets of God have nothing to do with them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r9.claim: Where Ṭāhā recounts only Moses, al-Anbiyā’ cites other prophets to highlight Qur’anic teachings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r9.anchor: In the previous sūrah, only the account of Moses (sws) was cited. In this one, accounts of other prophets are also cited.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r10.claim: The sūrah predicts truth’s dominance and the conquest of Makkah, warning Quraysh and giving Muslims glad tidings amid adversity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r10.anchor: the dominance of the truth and the conquest of Makkah are also predicted in an explicit way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r11.claim: The sūrah has three sections: it warns Quraysh, highlights Qur’anic truths through prophetic histories, then returns to the opening warning and their coming fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p90/r11.anchor: consists of three large sections. First the Quraysh are clearly warned of their foolish behaviour

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, as cited by al-Razi, al-Qurṭubī, and al-Zamakhsharī, takes الناس to mean the polytheists, as the following verses describe them.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس كما قال الإمام والقرطبي والزمخشري أن المراد بالناس المشركون

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r2.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r2.claim: Some eminent scholars say a generic الناس can remain generic when descriptions applying to a majority are attributed to all; the majority counts as the whole in law and custom.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة إن ما فيها من قبيل نسبة ما للبعض إلى الكل فلا ينافي كون تعريفه للجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r3.speaker: من الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r3.claim: Others allow the generic meaning, with subsequent pronouns referring to Meccan polytheists even though they were not previously named in this sūra.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r3.anchor: ومن الناس من جوز إرادة الجنس والضمائر فيها بعد لمشركي أهل مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r4.claim: Another view says the descriptions need not restrict the referent if they are read as traits shared by sinful monotheists too; al-Alusi says this departs far from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن دلالة ما ذكر على التخصيص ليست إلا على تقدير تفسير الأوصاف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r5.claim: The lām connects to اقترب, which takes the sense of approach to or from; some restrict it to إلى, but al-Alusi says both prepositions can mark an endpoint, with إلى more naturally doing so.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r5.anchor: واللام صلة لاقترب كما هو الظاهر وهو بمعنى إلى أو بمعنى من فإن ( اقترب ) افتعل من القرب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r6.claim: Ṣāḥib al-Kashf says من الناس works through a sense of specification or a starting point, either of which gives the intended meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r6.anchor: وفي الكشف المعنى على تقدير كونه صلة لاقترب من الناس لأن معنى الاختصاص وابتداء الغاية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi objects that min as a starting point does not fit its established uses here; it means an endpoint, as in تقربت منه being equivalent to تقربت إليه.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r7.anchor: فإن المفهوم منه أن يكون كلمة من التي يتعدى بها فعل الاقتراب بمعنى ابتداء الغاية وليس كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r8.speaker: الشمني وابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r8.claim: Al-Shumnī cites Ibn Mālik's example تقربت منه as equivalent to تقربت إليه; min can mark an endpoint, while إلى is not listed for a starting point.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r8.anchor: قال الشمني : وفي الجني الداني مثل ابن مالك لانتهاء الغاية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r9.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r9.claim: Al-Raḍī explains that a verb may take a preposition by analogy with its opposite, as البيع takes min after الشراء, which also takes min.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r9.anchor: وجعل تعديته بها حملا على ضده المتعدي بها وهو فعل البعد كما أن فعل البيع يعدى بمن

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r10.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r10.claim: Al-Baḥr says اقترب means قرب and is more emphatic because its form is longer.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r10.anchor: وحكى في البحر أنه أبلغ منه لزيادة مبناه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r11.claim: The approaching account means the approach of its time, the Hour; highlighting proximity rather than first occurrence makes resurrection and bodily revival seem self-evident despite the audience's denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r11.anchor: والمراد من اقتراب الحساب اقتراب زمانه وهو الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r12.claim: Speaking of the account's nearness is enough to evoke the Hour's frightening consequences; the point is that its time has drawn close, since the event itself needs no proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r12.anchor: بل نفس وقوع الحساب أيضا غني عن البيان لا ينبغي أن ترتاب فيه العقول والأذهان

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r1.claim: The verse may address polytheists who mockingly ask when the Hour will come; then its announcement of nearness directly answers their taunt.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الكلام مع المشركين السائلين عن زمان الساعة المستعجلين لها استهزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r2.claim: Mentioning the approaching account rather than the other consequences of resurrection warns that even a precursor of punishment should deter denial and arrogance, all the more so the punishment itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3/r2.anchor: مجرد اقتراب الحساب الذي هو من مبادي العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r1.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r1.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd says the account is named rather than the Hour because the discourse turns to their heedlessness and turning away from reminders; al-Alusi questions this explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r1.anchor: وذكر شيخ الإسلام مولانا أبو السعود عليه الرحمة إن إسناد ذلك إلى الحساب لا إلى الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r2.claim: Approach is attributed to whichever of two things moves toward the other, literally or figuratively; because time is conventionally viewed as coming to people, the account's time is the advancing subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r2.anchor: هو أن الاقتراب إذا حصل بين شيئين يسند إلى ما هو مقبل على الآخر متحرك ومتوجه إلى جهته

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r3.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd adds that assigning approach to the account magnifies and terrifies it by depicting it as an approaching force that pursues people and inevitably catches them; al-Alusi approves this added nuance.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r3.anchor: أن في هذا الإسناد من تفخيم شأن المسند إليه وتهويل أمره ما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r4.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r4.claim: On Abū al-Suʿūd's preferred view, the account draws nearer to people after being distant, becoming closer with each passing hour.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r4.anchor: والمراد من اقتراب ذلك من الناس على ما اختاره الشيخ قدس سره دنوه منهم بعد بعده عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains nearness as the remaining span of the world's life being shorter than what has passed, like the dregs left in a vessel.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r5.anchor: واعترض قول الزمخشري المراد من ذلك كون الباقي من مدة الدنيا أقل وأقصر مما مضى منها فإنه كصبابة الإناء ودردي الوعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi objects that this account of worldly duration is unnecessary to explain the past-tense approach or its basic meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r6.anchor: بأنه لا تعلق له بما نحن فيه من الاقتراب المستفاد من صيغة الماضي ولا حاجة إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r7.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r7.claim: A learned critic answers that reduced remaining duration is connected to the past-tense event, since the approach occurred as most of the world's lifetime passed; evidence places its onset at the Prophet's mission before revelation of the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p3#2/r7.anchor: وتعقبه بعض الأفاضل بأن القول بعدم التعلق بالإقتراب المستفاد من صيغة الماضي خارج عن دائرة الإنصاف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r1.claim: An objection says the proposed sense lacks contextual connection: if nearness has persisted from the world's beginning through and beyond revelation, an ongoing form would better express it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r1.anchor: فإن الإقتراب بذلك المعنى مستمر من أول بدء الدنيا إلى يوم نزول الآية بل إلى ما بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r2.claim: The objection says actual nearness is especially apt to the context, since it states the real closeness of the reckoning and threatens the disbelievers who doubt the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r2.anchor: هذا المعنى الذي اعترضه أنسب بما هو مقتضى المقام من إخافة الكفرة اللئام المرتابين في أمر القيام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r3.claim: One interpretation makes the reckoning near with God; its critic objects that created things cannot be near or far in relation to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد اقتراب ذلك عند الله تعالى وتعقب بأنه لا عند لله عز وجل إذ لا نسبة للكائنات إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r4.claim: The objection misunderstands the phrase: nearness with God means the reckoning is in His eternal knowledge or decree, not spatial or temporal proximity to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r4.anchor: فإن المراد من عند الله في علمه الأزلي أو في حكمه وتقديره لا الدنو والإقتراب المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r5.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r5.claim: A scholar explains nearness by God's perfect forbearance: long human eras are short by His measure, so the remaining time is truly brief and people should prepare.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r5.anchor: وقال بعض الأفاضل : ليس المراد من كون القرب عند الله تعالى نسبته إليه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r6.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r6.claim: Sheikh al-Islam rejects this reading here because proximity to God cannot change or renew; that consideration suits verses that do not assert an event's temporal occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r6.anchor: شيخ الإسلام في الإعتراض على ما قيل أنه لا سبيل إلى اعتباره ههنا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r7.claim: Another scholar takes nearness with God in its familiar idiomatic sense, as nearness in divine knowledge or decree, with renewal belonging to the relation, as in the raising of the Sleepers.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r7.anchor: اختار بعضهم أن المراد بالعندية ما سمعته أولا وهو معنى شائع في الإستعمال وجعل التجدد باعتبار التعلق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r8.claim: Another explanation is certain occurrence: whatever is coming is near, while what is distant is what has already passed; a poetic line illustrates the contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد من اقترابه تحقق وقوعه لا محالة فإن كل آت قريب والبعيد ما وقع ومضى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r9.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r9.claim: A scholar objects that certainty of occurrence does not explain the past-tense verb's implication of nearness unless the form is stripped of its eventive force, as in timeless praise formulas.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r9.anchor: وبعض الأفاضل قال : إنه على هذا الوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r10.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r10.claim: Fronting for people hastens the threat: associating the approach with the polytheists at the outset immediately distresses and frightens them.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r10.anchor: للمسارعة إلى إدخال الروعة فإن نسبة الإقتراب إلى المشركين من أول الأمر يسوؤهم ويورثهم رهبة وانزعاجا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r11.claim: Their heedlessness and turning away do not preclude fear: a warning can unsettle them if they entertain even a remote possibility that it is true.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p4/r11.anchor: في ذهنهم احتمال الصدق ولو مرجوحا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r1.claim: Some commentators report that after the earlier warning that the Hour was near, unbelievers paused some deeds, then mocked its delay; this verse made them fear and wait, but they later resumed mocking.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r2.claim: A rhetorician says approach suggests something advancing toward a target; adding for people makes them the pursued party fleeing it, which conveys danger and fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم في بيان ذلك : إن الإقتراب منبيء عن التوجه والإقبال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r3.claim: Putting for people before naming the reckoning delays identification of the terrifying approaching thing, letting the hearer imagine its horror; the reverse order would reveal the subject sooner.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r3.anchor: قيل ذكر الحساب بخلاف ما إذا قيل اقترب الحساب للناس فإن كون إقبال الحساب نحوهم لا يفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r4.claim: Another rationale is the Prophet's established practice of warning the polytheists: fronting for people signals from the start that the discourse concerns them and something distressing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r4.anchor: إن جريان عادته الكريمة صلى الله عليه وسلم على إنذار المشركين وتحذيرهم وبيان ما يزعجهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r5.claim: The argument relies on the Prophet's habit of speaking distressingly when discussing them, not a claim that most of his speech in all settings is distressing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5/r5.anchor: لا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام يتكلم في غالب أحواله بما يسوؤهم وفرق بين العادتين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.claim: Fronting aims to hasten the warning even if the audience does not in fact feel fear, just as a warning's intended effect remains its purpose when it fails.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r1.anchor: التقديم لتعجيل التخويف ولا ينافي ذلك عدم حصوله كما لا ينافي عدم حصول التخويف كون إنزال الآيات للتخويف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the lām as reinforcing the possessive relation: rather than deleting an annexed noun, the phrase uses a fronted locative predicate, followed by the definite reckoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r2.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون اللام تأكيدا لإضافة الحساب إليهم قال في الكهف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says fronting, the explicit lām, and the definite article add emphases absent from the basic wording; with their possessive force the lām reinforces restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r3.anchor: جوز الزمخشري كون اللام تأكيدا لإضافة الحساب إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.claim: Sheikh al-Islam and others criticize al-Zamakhshari's analysis as strained and contrary to the context; other scholars defend it, but the author prefers taking the lām as complement of approach.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r4.anchor: وادعى شيخ الإسلام أنه مع كونه تعسفا تاما بمعزل عما يقتضيه المقام وبحث فيه أيضا أبو حيان وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r5.claim: The verse establishes the reality of the reckoning; the author says reckoning as recompense is denied only by polytheists.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r6.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r6.claim: Al-Baydawi says Mu'tazilites and Kharijites deny the reckoning; al-Nasafi quotes Mu'tazilites denying the balance, reckoning, bridge, pool, and intercession, interpreting such references as justice.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r6.anchor: وذكر البيضاوي في تفسير قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r7.claim: The author notes that standard kalam works generally report most Mu'tazilites rejecting the bridge and all rejecting the balance, without mentioning rejection of the reckoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r7.anchor: أن أكثرهم بنفي الصراط وجميعهم ينفي الميزان ولم يتعرض فيها لنفيهم الحساب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r8.claim: One reading confines their profound ignorance to the approaching reckoning, while another includes ignorance of God, revelation, messengers, resurrection, reward, punishment, and all prophetic teaching.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r8.anchor: وقيل الأولى التعميم أي في غفلة تامة وجهالة عامة من توحيده تعالى والإيمان بكتبه ورسله

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r9.claim: Mentioning heedlessness after the reckoning does not restrict it to the reckoning, since their regret and ignorance will become evident on the Day of Reckoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r9.anchor: وذكر غفلتهم عن ذلك عقيب بيان اقتراب الحساب لا يقتضي قصر الغفلة عليه فإن وقوع تأسفهم وندامتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r10.claim: The author adds that anyone heedless of God's requital commits every kind of error and plunges into every kind of ignorance.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r10.anchor: ومن غفل عن مجازاة الله تعالى له المراد من الحساب صدر منه كل ضلالة وركب متن كل جهالة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r11.claim: The prepositional phrase belongs to an omitted predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p5#2/r11.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بمحذوف واقع خبرا لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r1.claim: The turning away is from signs and warnings that call them to saving faith; it is a second predicate alongside their being heedless.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r1.anchor: أي عن الآيات والنذر الناطقة بذلك الداعية إلى الإيمان به المنجي من المهالك خبر بعد خبر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari resolves the apparent tension by making them initially unaware of the outcome, then deliberately averse after warnings awaken them to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : وصفهم بالغفلة مع الإعراض على معنى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r3.claim: Al-Kashf says their persistent heedlessness concerns rational proofs; when scriptural proofs join them and they are guided to reflection, they turn away.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r3.anchor: وفي الكشف أراد أن حالهم المستمرة الغفلة عن مقتضى الأدلة العقلية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r4.claim: The nominal clause with a prepositional phrase conveys settled heedlessness, while the participial description of turning away indicates a renewed action; treating both as a single state is weaker.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r4.anchor: وفيه بيان فائدة إيراد الأول جملة ظرفية لما في حرف الظرف من الدلالة على التمكن

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r5.claim: The claim that reason itself requires reward and punishment works only with moral good and evil known by reason, which Ash'arites strongly deny.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r5.anchor: لا يتسنى إلا على القبول بالحسن والقبح العقليين والأشاعرة ينكرون ذلك أشد الإنكار

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r6.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r6.claim: Another scholar allows a sense of being extensive or excessive in heedlessness, supported by Arabic usage and the verse about turning away after rescue to land.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r6.anchor: وقال بعض الأفاضل : يمكن أن يحمل الإعراض على الإتساع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r7.claim: Heedlessness may also mean neglect, a usage that avoids contradiction between heedlessness and deliberate turning away.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p6/r7.anchor: ويمكن أيضا أن يراد بالغفلة معنى الإهمال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والقرطبي والزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Qurṭubī, and al-Zamakhsharī take “the people” to mean the polytheists, as the following verses describe them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r1.anchor: القرطبي والزمخشري أن المراد بالناس المشركون ويدل عليه ما ستسمعه بعد إن شاء الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r2.claim: One scholar says generic definiteness remains possible even if only some people are meant, because those people are the majority and the majority counts as the whole by custom and law.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r2.anchor: إن ما فيها من قبيل نسبة ما للبعض إلى كل فلا ينافي كون تعريفه للجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r3.claim: Others allow “people” to denote humanity generally while its later pronouns refer to the Meccan polytheists, although they have not yet been named in the sūra.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r3.anchor: ومن الناس من جوز إرادة الجنس والضمائر فيما بعد لمشركي أهل مكة وإن لم يتقدم ذكرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r4.claim: The argument that the descriptions specifically exclude monotheist sinners depends on narrow glosses of those descriptions; extending them to include such sinners is a very strained reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r4.anchor: ولا يخفى أن في ذلك ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r5.claim: The lām is governed by “approached” and can mean either “to” or “from,” since iqtaraba takes both prepositions.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r5.anchor: واللام صلة لا قترب كما هو الظاهر وهي معنى إلى أو بمعنى من

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r6.claim: Restricting the lām to the sense “to” is challenged as arbitrary; the author answers that both prepositions can mark an endpoint, though “to” is more characteristic of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r6.anchor: واقتصر بعضهم على القول بأنها بمعنى إلى فقيل فيه تحكم لحديث تعدي القرب بهما

ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r7.claim: The author concludes that min here denotes the endpoint, citing al-Shumnī and Ibn Mālik's Arabic example equating “approached from him” with “approached him”; min is listed with this meaning, unlike ilā as an origin marker.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p2/r7.anchor: فالحق أنها بمعنى انتهاء الغاية فانهم ذكروا أن من يجئ لذلك قال الشمني وفي الجنى الداني مثل ابن مالك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r1.speaker: اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r1.claim: Al-Lawāmiḥ says the wāw was dropped in connected recitation to avoid two sukūns, and spelling followed the pronunciation; a similar deletion appears in “yamḥu Allāhu al-bāṭil.”
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r1.anchor: وفي اللوامح أنها حذفت في الدرج لالتقاء الساكنين وحملت الكتابة على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r2.claim: The cited verse “If the doctors were around me” illustrates a written and pronounced missing wāw whose presence is indicated by ḍamma; some grammarians call the poetic usage necessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r2.anchor: وقد جاء حذف الواو لفظا وكتابة والإكتفاء بالضمة الدالة عليها كما في قوله : ولو أن الأطبا كان حولي وكان مع الأطباء الأساة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r3.claim: One gloss defines believers as those affirming what is necessarily known to belong to the Prophet's religion, including monotheism, prophethood, bodily resurrection, and recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3/r3.anchor: والمراد بالمؤمنين قيل إما المصدقون بما علم ضرورة أنه من دين نبينا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r1.claim: Some take the lām as meaning “from,” so the reckoning has drawn near to people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r1.anchor: قيل اللام بمعنى من، أي اقترب من الناس حسابهم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.claim: The approaching reckoning is God’s accounting of people’s deeds on the Day of Resurrection; the verse was revealed about deniers of resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r2.anchor: أي وقت محاسبة الله إياهم على أعمالهم، يعني يوم القيامة، نزلت في منكري البعث،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.claim: They are heedless of preparing for the reckoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p306#2/r3.anchor: في غفلة معرضون} عن التأهب له.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r1.claim: The account is near relative to what has passed or what is with God; all that is still to come is near, while only the past is distant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r1.anchor: اقترب للناس حسبهم } بالإضافة إلى ما مضى أو ما عند الله لقوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r2.claim: The lām may attach to اقترب or reinforce the possessive construction; the wording develops from people’s account to their account.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r2.anchor: واللام صلة ل { اقترب } أو تأكيد للإضافة وأصله اقترب حساب الناس

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r3.claim: “People” means unbelievers, identified by heedlessness about the account and turning away from reflection on it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r3.anchor: خص الناس بالكفار لتقييدهم بقوله: { وهم فى غفلة } أي في غفلة عن الحساب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r4.claim: Both “in heedlessness” and “turning away” are predicates; alternatively, the adverbial phrase is circumstantial with the subject of “turning away.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:1/r4.anchor: وهما خبران للضمير، ويجوز أن يكون الظرف حالا من المستكن في { معرضون }.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r1.claim: The opening names God as wise and just with complete power and command, Allah as the unrivaled King, the All-Merciful as giving all creation the mercy of existence, and the Merciful as saving whom He wills in the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r1.anchor: الحكيم العدل الذي تمت قدرته وعم أمره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r2.claim: TaHa ends warning that people will learn who is wretched and who is blessed; Anbiya opens with the clearest realization of that warning, the Day of Reckoning when the veil is fully lifted and knowledge becomes direct sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r2.anchor: لما ختمت طه بإنذارهم بأنهم سيعلمون الشقي والسعيد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r3.claim: The account is the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection; ḥisāb also means enumerating something and requiting it with good or evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r3.anchor: والحساب : إحصاء الشيء والمجازاة عليه بخير أو شر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r4.claim: The iftiʿāl form intensifies the nearness because no later community remains whose turn must first arrive.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r4.anchor: بصيغة الافتعال غلى مزيد القرب لأنه لا أمة بعد هذه ينتظر أمرها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r5.claim: Delaying the subject their account heightens suspense by letting the listener imagine what is approaching.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r5.anchor: وأخر الفاعل تهويلا لتذهب النفس في تعيينه كل مذهب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, account can mean recompense, making the verse a threat of events such as Badr and the Conquest, with people referring to Quraysh or all Arabs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r6.anchor: ويصح أن يراد بالحساب الجزاء , فيكون ذلك تهديدا بيوم بدر والفتح ونحوهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r7.claim: On the primary reading, people means everyone generally, including the addressees and others.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r8.claim: The word nās is associated with naws, restlessness that prevents people from remaining secure and steady; only very few are saved from this deficiency.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r8.anchor: من أجل ما في جبلاتهم من النوس , وهو الاضطراب الموجب لعدم الثبات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r9.claim: Their heedlessness is exposed when they are raised, or when events kill them and leave survivors humbled, so that they recognize truth and falsehood.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r9.anchor: لأنهم إذا نشروا علموت , وإذا أبادتهم الوقائع علموا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r10.claim: Turning away from God’s warnings causes their heedlessness; the closing confession that they were wrongdoers will confirm this, though reason already requires requital of good and evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r10.anchor: أحاطت بهم الغفلة بسبب إعراضهم عما يأتيهم منا , وسيأتي ما يؤيد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the near account to the preceding warning not to covet worldly goods: their abundance is a trial and people will answer for every blessing, so the reckoning is near.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r1.anchor: أي لا تمدن عينيك إلى ذلك فإني جعلته فتنة لمن ناله بغير حق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r2.claim: The earlier warning about a contentious people and destruction of past generations called for fuller consolation and explanation, which this sūra supplies.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r3.claim: TaHa consoles the Prophet with the assurance that the Qur’an was not sent to make him suffer, then with Moses’ struggle against Pharaoh, his ruin, and the inheritance of his land by God’s servants.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r4.claim: The story of Adam and his struggle with Iblis also comforts Muhammad: it shows that hardship from an adversary is God’s established way with His servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r4.anchor: ثم اتبعت بقصة آدم عليه السلام ليرى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r5.claim: Anbiya continues this consolation by showing the approaching Judgment and good outcome of striving for God, whose reward makes even greater hardship desirable.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r5.anchor: فبين اقتراب الحساب ووقوع يوم الفصل المحمود فيه ثمرة ما كوبد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r6.claim: After its consolation, the sūra presents admonitions, proofs, and signs, and recalls God’s established practice of destroying earlier communities that did not believe.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p64/r6.anchor: وأعلم أنه سبحانه قد سبقت سنته بإهلاك من لم يكن منه الإيمان

DURR-FULL:v5p615/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r1.claim: The author identifies Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ as Meccan and says it has 112 verses.

DURR-FULL:v5p615/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة الأنبياء بمكة

DURR-FULL:v5p615/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr likewise reports that Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r3.anchor: عن ابن الزبير قال: نزلت سورة الأنبياء بمكة

DURR-FULL:v5p615/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p615/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
